candidate.candidate_scope: Recycle confirmation alpha only after a prior candidate passes a fresh conditionally valid confirmation, using Online Fallback/Fallback-1 style transfer; worker-local simulations additionally compare geometric and polynomial base schedules.

published_sources.title: Online control of the familywise error rate
published_sources.identifier: arXiv:1910.04900 / Statistical Methods in Medical Research 30(4):976-993
published_sources.published_claim_scope: For an a priori unbounded sequence of hypotheses, Online Fallback chooses base gamma mass plus transfer from previous rejections. Proposition 2 states strong FWER control for arbitrarily dependent p-values. Online Fallback-1 is the special case alpha_i = alpha*gamma_i + R_{i-1}*alpha_{i-1}.

published_sources.title: Family-wise Error Rate Control with E-values
published_sources.published_claim_scope: E-value closed testing and e-Fallback for a fixed set of hypotheses, with stronger sequential/always-valid properties across time for that fixed family. The latest text explicitly distinguishes online closed testing with sequentially arriving hypotheses from this paper's fixed-family setting.

tian_ramdas_repository.readme_claim: Repository contains code for the online FWER algorithms and commands to reproduce all paper figures.

fallback1_implementation.mechanical_match: Exact source recurrence is alpha_1=gamma_1 and alpha_k=gamma_k + R_{k-1}*alpha_{k-1}, with gamma already scaled by alpha0; computeFWER.py maps this class to algorithm 6 Online Fallback-1.

general_fallback_implementation.mechanical_match: General rejected alpha is redistributed to future tests according to a normalized transfer sequence.

reproducibility_limits: No dependency lock or environment manifest was observed in the inspected source path.
The repository uses older scientific-Python idioms in some files (for example np.float in recycling_FWER.py), so a modern environment may require compatibility edits.

The worker's geometric gamma schedule is not the default power-law gamma used by the official repository; the theorem permits general summable gamma, but paper-code numerical outputs are not a replay of the worker's geometric schedule.

official_fallback1_null_sanity.method: Reimplemented the exact public saving_FWER.py recurrence and its source gamma normalization in an independent Python harness.
official_fallback1_null_sanity.interpretation: The independent source-level rerun matches the expected all-null FWER for the exact published-code recurrence. This is a mechanism sanity check, not a proof of strong FWER with mixed null/non-null configurations or arbitrary dependence.

separate_public_implementation.implementation_scope: A separate public Python package implements the same adjacent-rejection recurrence alpha_t = alpha0*gamma_t + previous_alpha when the previous test rejected.
separate_public_implementation.tests_observed: tests/test_statistical_sanity.py includes a 150-run x 400-null-stream sanity check requiring empirical FWER <= 1.25*alpha; test_parity_regressions.py includes boundary behavior for OnlineFallback.
separate_public_implementation.scope_guard: This is separate implementation-level support, not a protocol-matched reproduction of Tian-Ramdas Figure 3 or the worker's confirmation-stream simulation; its default gamma sequence also differs.

scope_correction.hartog_lei_fixed_family_boundary: The latest Hartog-Lei text explicitly says online closed testing where hypotheses arrive sequentially differs from their setting with a fixed set of hypotheses. Therefore their e-Fallback/always-valid results do not by themselves validate direct insertion into an unbounded adaptively generated candidate-identity stream.
scope_correction.safe_interface_statement: Tian-Ramdas directly supports p-value Online Fallback-1 on an unbounded hypothesis stream. If each fresh confirmation yields a p-value that is valid under the required history-conditional null and alpha/gamma/transfer choices are predictable, the worker's p-value fallback interface is source-aligned.
scope_correction.unsafe_overclaim: Do not cite Hartog-Lei e-Fallback as direct proof that an adaptively growing family of newly generated candidate identities has lifetime strong FWER. That transfer needs an online closed-testing result or a fresh conditional-e-value derivation specific to arriving hypotheses.

assessment.overall_grade: B+ for the worker candidate as an auditable confirmation-stream mechanism
assessment.hartog_lei_direct_adaptive_identity_tran: C/not supported by the cited fixed-family result
assessment.reasoning: The core p-value Online Fallback-1 mechanism is unusually well supported: the theorem explicitly covers an unbounded stream and arbitrary p-value dependence, the paper-linked code implements the exact adjacent-rejection recurrence, an independent source-level null sanity check agrees with its expected behavior, and a separate public package implements the same recurrence. The remaining uncertainty is not the fallback recurrence itself but the worker-specific confirmation-stream simulation and any attempt to use Hartog-Lei e-Fallback directly for adaptively arriving hypothesis identities.

downstream_scope_guard.safe_positive_statement: Online Fallback-1 is a source-supported strong-FWER recycling mechanism for an unbounded p-value stream, and the exact adjacent-rejection recurrence used by the evaluation worker matches the paper-linked implementation.
downstream_scope_guard.safe_negative_statement: The sealed worker artifact does not make its exact 100,000-run stress numbers independently replayable, and Hartog-Lei's e-Fallback is a fixed-family result rather than a direct theorem for adaptively arriving candidate identities.
do_not_generalize: Do not infer that any marginally valid p-value remains valid after adaptive candidate generation; the worker's stronger fresh conditional-null requirement remains material.
Do not infer that the worker's geometric-vs-polynomial power ranking is universal; it is simulation-regime dependent.
Do not infer that fixed-family e-Fallback automatically gives lifetime FWER for an unbounded adaptive hypothesis stream.
